workingTitle: A new galaxy model explains how early stars could form in bursts
publicationStatus: Unreviewed arXiv preprint, first submitted October 7, 2026
coreFacts: SAGE26 updates the semi-analytic SAGE galaxy-evolution model with five observationally motivated improvements.
A feedback-free starburst pathway helps the model produce massive high-redshift galaxies at abundances seen by JWST.
The model distinguishes free-fall-limited gas inflow in low-mass halos from hydrostatic cooling in massive halos.
SAGE26 reproduces the stellar mass function and cosmic star-formation rate density across cosmic time.
Code and data products are reported as open-source and publicly available.
caveats: Model predictions and population-level fits, not direct observations of feedback-free star formation in a specific galaxy.
Agreement with aggregate observations does not uniquely establish the physical assumptions.

sources.label: Bradley et al., SAGE26 Paper I, arXiv preprint
